attributes.residual: ONE SMALL GAIN RETAINED, THE HEADLINE AXIS REFUTED. Retained: `u8* hdr2;` in the case-29 arm was declared and never used; deleting it moved the frame 216 -> 208 and the low region 80 -> 76 with real flat at 191 and the opcode stream untouched (commit 53fae5ed5). Baseline geometry re-measured: target frame 160 / low 16, ours (after the deletion) 208 / 76; the three low locals sit at ours 84/88/92 against target 24/28/32 and the fourth referenced slot tracks the frame delta exactly. THE PARKED RECORD'S NEXT AXIS IS REFUTED AS STATED. It predicted that hoisting inner-block declarations to function scope 'should drain the low region toward target's 16 bytes', budgeting roughly 14 four-byte declarations. Hoisting the most-repeated group - the `u8* ep; Effect* e;` pair plus the `f32 k1;` that recur identically in all four switch arms (case 29, case 24, default, case 25), 3 declarations x 4 arms - drained the low region by only FOUR BYTES (84 -> 80), left the frame at 208, and regressed real 191 -> 209 with a new target-only `+1 add`. CAUSE, and the reason the arithmetic in the park was wrong: the switch arms are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE, so MWCC already OVERLAYS their inner-block locals in the low region - the region is sized by the LARGEST arm (case 29's ~14 declarations = 56 bytes), not by the sum across arms. Hoisting a per-arm declaration to function scope therefore removes only ONE arm's worth from the overlay while adding a permanently-live slot to the named area above, which is net-neutral on the frame and destroys the deliberate `ep` address web that the function's own source comment records as a prior fix. TO DRAIN THIS LOW REGION one must reduce the declaration count of the LARGEST ARM specifically (case 29: nb, r2, ep, e, k1, n2, hdr, at, y, yp, ro2, mp2, pv, t0), not hoist declarations that repeat across arms - and every one of those is a live address web on a 342-instruction function whose opcode stream is already within 1 token of target, so the next agent should expect to trade real for frame and must arbitrate on slotdiff, not real.
